Nxeon codebase at /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TS/Prisma). I'm planning a new feature: give paid Minecraft game servers a friendly domain (`<hostname>.playmc.nxeon.cloud`) via a DNS SRV record pointing at the server's actual `ip:port`, instead of customers connecting via raw `sharedPublicIp:forwardedPort`.

I need to know every place in the codebase where a game server's effective `ip:port` for the game protocol can CHANGE after initial provisioning, so I know where to re-sync the DNS record. Specifically, research and report back (read-only, no edits):

1. **Port-forward CRUD for a server's game port**: `lib/actions-server.ts` has port-forward add/edit/delete server actions (used by `components/customer/NetworkingControls.tsx` per app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx's imports: `AddForwardForm, DeleteForwardButton`, etc.). Find the exact function(s) that create/update/delete a `PortForward` row. Is there a single function all mutations funnel through (a good single choke point to hook a DNS-resync call into), or are they scattered? Get exact function names and file:line.

2. **Dedicated IP assignment/removal**: is there an admin or customer action that assigns/removes a `DedicatedIp` from a `Server` after initial provisioning (not just at order time)? Find it if it exists (grep `dedicatedIp`, `DedicatedIp` assignment mutations outside of provision()).

2b. Also check: does provisioning ever auto-create a `PortForward` for the game's own port (e.g. mapping the shared NAT IP's some port -> guest 25565), or per the note "a game's own port is forwarded only if the customer adds one" is it purely manual? I want to confirm whether a fresh Minecraft server on a NAT (non-dedicated-IP) node is actually reachable at all before the customer manually adds a forward, since that affects whether DNS-record creation at provision-time even has a valid ip:port to point at yet for non-dedicated-IP servers.

3. **Server migration/resize** (`worker/migrate.ts` or similar) — does migrating a server to a new node ever change its public IP (for non-dedicated-IP servers, if the new node has a different NAT public IP)? Find the relevant code path and confirm whether existing code already has a "this server's public IP changed, update dependent things" pattern I could hook into (e.g. does it already update DNS for anything else, like the site-builder's per-site domain, when a site's backing server migrates?).

4. **worker/index.ts's `provision()` function** — confirm the EXACT variable names in scope right after the "game port open" check succeeds (the insertion point identified as around line ~690, before `status: "RUNNING"` is set ~line 704) for: the server's hostname, its effective public IP (dedicated or NAT), and the actual game port number that will work externally. I need exact variable names so a `upsertGameServerDns({ hostname, ip, port })`-style call can be written directly against them without guessing.

5. Confirm whether `Server.hostname` is guaraneed non-null, DNS-label-safe (only `[a-z0-9-]`), and globally unique across ALL servers (not just within a family) — I want to use it directly as the DNS subdomain label with zero new validation/schema needed. Check wherever `hostname` is generated at order/provision time (probably `lib/game-order.ts` or `worker/index.ts`) for its exact character set and uniqueness guarantee.

Report back concisely with file:line citations and exact variable/function names — this feeds directly into an implementation plan, so precision matters more than prose.

All paths below are relative to `/opt/nxeon` (that's the actual repo root — `/opt/nxeon/app` is just the Next.js `app/` router directory, not a separate project).

## 1. Port-forward CRUD — scattered mutations, but ONE re-sync choke point (global, not per-server)

`lib/actions-server.ts`:
- `addPortForward(prev, formData)` — lines 252–323. Creates a `PortForward` row at line 298 (`db.portForward.create`), then at **line 317** enqueues `db.job.create({ data: { type: "SYNC_FORWARDS", serverId } })`.
- `deletePortForward(serverId, forwardId)` — lines 325–333. Deletes at line 327 (`db.portForward.deleteMany`), then at **line 328** enqueues the same `SYNC_FORWARDS` job.
- **There is no `updatePortForward`/edit function.** `components/customer/NetworkingControls.tsx` only imports/uses `addPortForward` and `deletePortForward` (confirmed also in `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx:24`, which imports `AddForwardForm, DeleteForwardButton` from that same file). "Editing" a forward in the UI is add+delete.
- No other file mutates `db.portForward` (`grep` confirmed).

**The choke point is the `SYNC_FORWARDS` job**, not a shared function — both actions independently create it. Handled at `worker/index.ts:1394`: `SYNC_FORWARDS: async () => { if (!SANDBOX) await syncPortForwards(); }`. **Important caveat: `syncPortForwards()` (`worker/network.ts:89`) is a global, fleet-wide reconciliation** — it reads `db.server.findMany(...)` for every non-suspended/non-deleting server with an IP+sshPort and rebuilds the whole iptables NAT chain from `planNatRules()`. It is not scoped to the one server that changed. If you hook DNS re-sync onto `SYNC_FORWARDS`, you'd need to either scope it to `job.serverId` yourself or accept it firing a full-fleet DNS diff. A cleaner hook is directly in `addPortForward`/`deletePortForward` themselves, right where each creates its `SYNC_FORWARDS` job (lines 317 and 328) — that's the actual per-server CRUD boundary.

## 2. Dedicated IP assignment/removal outside provision — yes, in two places

`lib/dedicated-ip.ts`:
- `allocateDedicatedIp(serverId, vmid)` (163–215) and `releaseDedicatedIp(serverId)` (218–235) are the primitives.

Two callers mutate a server's dedicated IP **after** initial provisioning:
1. **Admin action** `releaseIpFromServer(ipId)` — `lib/actions-ovh.ts:55-62`. Admin-only, calls `releaseDedicatedIp(server.id)` directly against a live server (e.g. from `/admin/ips`). This releases the IP but does **not** allocate a replacement — the server is left on whatever `Server.ipAddress` remains stale in the DB unless something else reconfigures it (worth flagging: this admin path looks like it can desync the DB from the actual VM network config; out of scope for your feature but relevant since it also invalidates any DNS record).
2. **Suspend/unsuspend cycle** — `worker/index.ts`, function `suspend(job, unsuspend)` (starts line 924):
   - On **suspend** (lines 990–1005): if the server holds a dedicated IP, it's released back to the pool via `releaseDedicatedIp(server.id)` (line 996), then `Server.ipAddress`/`ipv6` are nulled (lines 1001–1004).
   - On **unsuspend** (lines 935–975): if dedicated-by-default and no IP currently held, it **re-allocates a (possibly different) dedicated IP** via `allocateDedicatedIp(server.id, server.vmid)` (line 945), reconfigures Proxmox `net0`/`ipconfig0` (947–950), and writes the new address back: `db.server.update({ ..., data: { ipAddress: d.address, sshPort: null } })` (**line 951**). If dedicated re-allocation isn't possible, it falls back to NAT with a freshly allocated `ip`/`sshPort` (lines 964–970, written at line 970).

**This is the single most important non-provision-time IP-change path** — a paid Minecraft server that gets suspended for non-payment and later unsuspended can come back with a genuinely different public IP (and, on the NAT fallback, a different `sshPort`, though that's irrelevant to the game port itself).

## 2b. Confirmed: NAT servers get NO automatic forward for the game port — only SSH

`worker/provision-health.ts:236-242` (comment on `checkGamePortOpen`) and `worker/index.ts:675-681`/`691-693` state it explicitly and consistently:

> "Only SSH gets an automatic NAT port-forward at provision time (`syncPortForwardsBestEffort`); the game's own port is forwarded only if the customer adds a `PortForward` for it (`lib/actions-server.ts`) — a separate, pre-existing product gap this task does not touch."

Confirmed by the code itself: `worker/index.ts:606` — `if (!SANDBOX && !dedicated) natError = await syncPortForwardsBestEffort(...)` runs `syncPortForwards()`, which reconciles the DB's existing `PortForward` rows into iptables. Since no `PortForward` row exists yet for a freshly-created server, nothing gets DNAT'd for the game port on a NAT node. The health check at line 682 (`checkGamePortOpen(ip, game.port, game.protocol)`) deliberately checks against the **internal/guest** `ip`, not a public address, precisely because there's no public mapping to test yet.

**Consequence for your feature**: for a non-dedicated-IP (NAT) Minecraft server, there is genuinely no valid external `ip:port` at provision time — DNS-record creation must be deferred until the customer adds a `PortForward` (i.e., hooked into `addPortForward` in `lib/actions-server.ts`, not into `provision()`). Only dedicated-IP servers have a usable `ip:port` (the guest port itself, unmapped) immediately at provision time.

## 3. Migration — no internal node-to-node migration exists; resize never touches IP

- `worker/migrate.ts` / `worker/migrate-real.ts` / `worker/migrate-detect.ts` are **not** an Nxeon-server-to-Nxeon-node migration feature. They implement a **cross-provider lift-and-shift**: pulling files/DBs from a customer's *external* VPS (SSH) onto their *already-provisioned* Nxeon server (`lib/actions-migrate.ts` enqueues `MIGRATE` jobs against a `Migration` row with `sourceHost`/`sourcePort` etc., see `worker/migrate.ts:44-72`, `85-98`). It never changes the target `Server`'s `nodeId`/`ipAddress`/`sshPort` — grepping `migrate-real.ts` (9412 lines) for `ipAddress`/`nodeId`/`server.update` returns **zero hits**; it only reads `target.dedicatedIp?.address` (`migrate-real.ts:5171`, `7828`) to know where to SSH.
- I found **no** "move this server to a different node" feature anywhere (`grep` for `moveServer`, `relocateServer`, `changeNode`, `migrateNode` — nothing).
- `lib/resize.ts` (`resizeQuote`/`applyResize`, used by `lib/actions-server.ts:resizeServer`) never references `nodeId`, `ipAddress`, or `sshPort` — a plan resize is same-node, same-IP, confirmed.
- **So: today, the only path that changes an existing provisioned server's public IP is the suspend/unsuspend cycle in #2.** There is no "server's public IP changed, update dependent things" pattern already in the codebase for internal migrations, because internal migration doesn't exist yet.
- The closest existing "DNS gets updated when a backing thing changes" pattern is `worker/migrate.ts`'s `runPostCutoverTls`/`postCutoverTlsSweep` (lines 274-369, 523-581) — but that's the *inverse* direction: it waits for the **customer's own external DNS** (for their own registered domain, via their own Cloudflare token) to be repointed at the new Nxeon server, then issues a Let's Encrypt cert. Nxeon does not write that DNS record itself; it only detects when the customer has and reacts. **There is no existing code path where Nxeon programmatically creates/updates a DNS record for one of its own zones in response to an internal server-address change.** You'd be building that pattern from scratch (see the reusable primitive in point 5b below).

## 4. `provision()` exact variables at the insertion point

Confirmed in `worker/index.ts`. The insertion point (right after the game-port check passes, before the `RUNNING` status write) is exactly where you described:

```
666:    const game = gamePortForServer(server as unknown as ServerFamilyLike);
667:    if (game) {
674:      await step("Starting the game server…");
682:      const gameCheck = await checkGamePortOpen(ip, game.port, game.protocol);
683:      if (!gameCheck.ok) { throw new Error(...); }
690:      }                                    // <-- gameCheck.ok is true here
691:    } else if (server.gamePlanId) { ... }
701:    }
702:  }
703:
704:  const runningServer = await db.server.update({ where: { id: server.id }, data: { status: "RUNNING", provisioningStep: null } });
```

Variables in scope at line 690 (inside `if (game) {...}`, still inside the outer `if (!SANDBOX) {...}` starting at 649):

| Need | Variable | Defined at | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| hostname | `server.hostname` | loaded via `loadServer(job)` earlier | string, immutable post-creation (see #5) |
| dedicated-IP flag/address | `dedicated` | `worker/index.ts:486` (`let dedicated: {address, virtualMac, gateway} \| null = null`), set at line 494 via `allocateDedicatedIp` | `dedicated.address` = the real public IP, only when a dedicated IP was granted |
| "public-ish" IP used for the game-port check | `ip` | `worker/index.ts:501`: `const ip = dedicated ? dedicated.address : (server.ipAddress ?? await allocateIp(...))` | **For dedicated servers this IS the public IP.** For NAT servers this is the guest's private/node-internal address, NOT what a customer would connect to. |
| the actual customer-facing public host for NAT | `server.node?.publicIp ?? process.env.PUBLIC_IP` | used explicitly at `worker/index.ts:654` (`sshHost`) — reuse the same expression | Only meaningful for SSH there; the *game port* is not yet forwarded to it (see #2b) |
| game's listen port/protocol | `game.port`, `game.protocol` | `worker/index.ts:666`: `const game = gamePortForServer(server as unknown as ServerFamilyLike)` → from `lib/games.ts:80`: `minecraft: { port: 25565, protocol: "tcp" }` | This is the **guest-internal** port; it equals the externally-usable port only when `dedicated` is truthy |

**Net for a `upsertGameServerDns({ hostname, ip, port })` call inserted at line 690/691**:
- Only call it when `dedicated` is truthy: `upsertGameServerDns({ hostname: server.hostname, ip: dedicated!.address, port: game.port })`.
- When `!dedicated` (NAT), there is nothing valid to point DNS at yet — per #2b, skip it here entirely and instead create/update the DNS record inside `addPortForward` (`lib/actions-server.ts`) once the customer adds a forward whose `guestPort === game.port`, using `server.node?.publicIp ?? process.env.PUBLIC_IP` and the forward's `publicPort`.

## 5. `Server.hostname` — NOT unique, NOT guaranteed collision-free, but is DNS-label-safe and immutable

`prisma/schema.prisma:497-566` (`model Server`): `hostname String` — **line 505, no `@unique`, no `@@unique`, no index at all.** Only `vmid` (506), `ipAddress` (508), and `sshPort` (509) carry `@unique` on this model. Confirmed via `awk` extraction of the whole model block — `hostname` appears exactly once, as a bare column.

Generation/validation, `lib/game-order.ts`:
- `HOSTNAME_RE = /^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$/i` (line 100) — applied to an already-lowercased string (line 220: `.trim().toLowerCase()`), length gated to 3–40 (line 224). This **is** a valid DNS label character set (no leading/trailing hyphen, `[a-z0-9-]` body) — good news for using it as a label with zero new charset validation.
- Auto-generated case: `hostname = \`${gp.gameFamily}-${randSuffix()}\`` (line 223), `randSuffix()` (102-105) = 6 random base-36 chars (`Math.random().toString(36)`) — **probabilistic, not DB-checked** for collisions.
- Customer-supplied case (lines 220-228): validated **only** for charset/length — **there is no `findFirst`/`findUnique` uniqueness check against existing hostnames anywhere in this function or in `lib/order.ts`** (grepped both files for `findFirst`/`findUnique` near "host" — zero hits). Two different customers (or the same customer twice) can create servers with the identical hostname today, with no error.
- Immutability: `lib/actions-server-extra.ts:renameServer` (20-40+) only ever writes `Server.label` (the display nickname), never `Server.hostname`. Grepped the whole repo for any hostname-mutating action (`renameServer|updateHostname|setHostname`) — only that one function exists, and it doesn't touch `hostname`. So once set, `hostname` never changes — no rename-driven DNS resync needed.

**Bottom line for your plan: you cannot use `Server.hostname` directly as a global DNS label with "zero new validation/schema."** It's DNS-safe on charset alone, but it is **not unique** — neither DB-enforced nor app-enforced, across all servers or even within one user's account beyond a hard block on the exact same string existing twice for that same user (there isn't even that). You'll need one of: (a) a new DB-level `@@unique` constraint on `hostname` plus a pre-create collision check (retconning existing duplicate rows first), or (b) compose the DNS label as `hostname-{server.id.slice(...)}` or similar to sidestep the uniqueness gap without a migration, or (c) add a dedicated new unique column (e.g. `dnsSlug`) rather than repurposing `hostname`.

## Bonus: existing DNS-upsert code you can reuse/extend

`lib/cloudflare-dns.ts` already implements exactly the "upsert" pattern you'd want (`cfUpsertRecords(token, zoneId, records)`, lines 174-209): look up existing record by type+name, `PUT` to update in place or `POST` to create. **However it only supports `CfRecordType = "TXT" | "MX" | "A"` (line 113)** — no `SRV` support yet (Cloudflare's API needs a `data: {priority, weight, port, target}` object for SRV rather than the flat `content` string this module builds at lines 189-197), so it needs extending, not reusing as-is. It's also built for **customer-supplied** Cloudflare tokens (top-of-file comment, line 5-7) — for `*.playmc.nxeon.cloud` you'd need Nxeon's own API token for its own zone, which today I found only as an inert reference: `.env.bak-1786835428:46`, "Cloudflare zone-DNS token for `*.sites.nxeon.cloud` wildcard TLS (inert until `HOSTING_WILDCARD_SSL=1`...)" — i.e. a similar token exists in principle for a different, currently-unused wildcard-TLS feature, but nothing wires it up for live DNS record management today. You'd be adding a new "Nxeon-operated zone" credential/config, separate from the existing customer-token flow in `lib/cloudflare-dns.ts`.
